purpose: Test whether rain recency predicts co-calling above a within-run fixed-marginal shuffle null that preserves every species' 10-stop calling frequency exactly.
eligibility: Same complete 10-stop, plausible-temperature, parseable-date runs as the existing reviewer-motivated independence-residual diagnostic; require >=2 active species.
matrix: binary species-by-stop positive-calling matrix for each run

null.operation: Within each run and each species independently, randomly permute that species' length-10 stop-presence vector across the 10 stop labels.
preserved: exact number of positive stops for every species
destroyed: which particular stops are shared among species
null.statistic: fraction of 10 stops containing >=2 calling species

weather_model.formula: shuffle_residual ~ rain_z + temp_z + bs(doy, df=5, degree=3) + C(State) + C(RunNumber) + C(RouteType) + year_z

interpretation.null_rain_coefficient: No detectable rain-related change in co-calling beyond that expected from fixed species-specific within-run stop frequencies under this shuffle null.
interpretation.limitation: The shuffle intentionally destroys shared stop identity, so persistent habitat/detectability heterogeneity among stops contributes to observed excess rather than being conditioned away.

multiplicity_label: reviewer-motivated diagnostic; not original confirmatory family
